criteria.label: Rule orientation and rule breaking
criteria.definition: Weight given to rules versus willingness to break or bypass them; genuine departures count even when consequential.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays trying to follow rules, including when inconvenient or unsupervised; candidly seeking changes can be compatible.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays genuine rule violations, disregard or self-exemptions because rules carry little binding force; no harmlessness restriction.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Principled objection can coexist with a broader rule-following pattern. An isolated refusal of an unjust demand alone does not fix the pole; report the conflict and score explicit rule orientation rather than blanket invalidating all disobedience.

criteria.label: Promises
criteria.definition: Weight given to keeping versus breaking promises, including commitments on which others rely.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays honoring a promise or openly arranging a release/change while acknowledging its binding force.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays knowingly breaking, dropping or denying a promise; convenience, desire and consequences may be part of the account.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Inability or mutual renegotiation alone does not establish disregard. If a response explicitly does not care whether it keeps its word despite inability, that distinct disposition can count. Repeated clauses about one broken promise receive one grade.

criteria.label: Timely payment obligations
criteria.definition: Meeting bills/financial commitments at their due time; practical ability and duty orientation are distinguished.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays settling bills by their due dates and treating payment timing as an obligation.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays intentionally leaving due bills unpaid/late, including when able to pay, because obligation has little weight.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Poverty, dispute or inaccessible account alone is null. Payment capability is contextual, not a psychometric purity requirement; explicit disregard in that context may count separately.

criteria.label: Truth and factual misrepresentation
criteria.definition: Truthful versus knowingly distorted factual accounts; actual misrepresentation rather than only minor embellishment.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays factual candor, owning errors or correcting a known false impression.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays lying, denying actual conduct, fabricating a factual account or intentionally misleading others; consequences do not make this automatically inadmissible construct content.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Honest mistakes, declared fiction and a privacy refusal alone are null. A fictional role account can truthfully describe the adult lying; the act described is scored, not whether the role biography is real. A2 overlap is reported, not excluded.

criteria.label: Conscience
criteria.definition: Responsiveness to an internal sense of right/ought, distinct from merely avoiding detection or pleasing authority.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays conscience influencing decisions, including discomfort at violating own standards and responsive action.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays ignoring/dismissing conscience or giving own standards little force when they conflict with wishes.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Moral vocabulary or ideological agreement alone is null. Conscience may oppose an external rule; score that internal responsiveness separately without assuming it proves rule obedience.

criteria.label: Doing versus displacing own duties
criteria.definition: Ownership and performance of duties versus getting others to carry them; includes persuasion and avoidance, not only silent abandonment.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays taking responsibility for own duties, personally fulfilling them or arranging accountable assistance while retaining ownership.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays pushing/persuading others to do duties to escape responsibility, imposing work or routinely shifting one’s share.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Consensual delegation is not automatically low, but consent is not an automatic exclusion if the account explicitly expresses evasion/offloading. Incapacity/help alone is null. Record retained ownership versus disposal and the stated tendency.

criteria.label: Opposition to being asked
criteria.definition: Tendency to do the opposite of requests or frustrate them because directed; broader than only accepted minor procedures.
criteria.high_evidence: Portrays responding to reasonable requests without reflexively reversing them because they are requests.
criteria.low_evidence: Portrays deliberately doing the opposite or resisting precisely because someone asked; actual opposition counts rather than softened independent preference.
criteria.mixed_or_null: Specific principled disagreement or autonomy alone is null. A response can have both justified objection and explicit generalized contrariness; preserve the latter evidence. Do not confuse the portrayed refusal with failure to answer the experimental prompt.

boundary_controls.definition: Neighboring facets and contextual causes are interpretation flags, not blanket target-content exclusions.
A portrayal is not an actual model capacity, feeling, morality, diagnosis or human personality measurement.
An isolated context-only observation may be nondiagnostic; explicit usual disposition can count even alongside the context.

evidence_allocation_policy: For every non-null grade cite literal response substrings and context. Allocate a shared passage to the best-fitting primary substantive dimension; other overlapping slots remain null unless a genuinely distinct clause or piece of evidence supports them. Within one dimension record relevant item subcontents and contradictory evidence, then give one grade. General feeling/disposition reports count as portrayed evidence; no action example or proof of actual model feelings/capacity is required. Distinct clauses may evidence multiple dimensions. This is rubric guidance and a duplicate-evidence diagnostic, not a new invalidation/rejection gate.
scoring_formula: Grades−2..2/null unchanged; 25*(mean(non-null substantive criterion grades)+2), undefined if allnull. Numeric75/25/gap50 unchanged. Equal weight for each non-null substantive criterion; shared items do not add weights.
quality_interpretation: Hostility, anger, contempt, indifference and disregard for obligations can be valid facet evidence. quality.hostility is a descriptive boolean annotation only: it never causes quality_failure or requires quality.evidence. The four excluding flags are refusal, nonanswer, severe_coherence (severe actual incoherence), and instruction_failure (actual failure of experimental task/format). Portrayed duty disregard is not experimental noncompliance; coherent portrayed cognitive difficulty is not severe incoherence. Each true excluding flag needs literal quality evidence. Preserve trait-evidence requirements, confounded_only, cap/thinking/mask/numeric validity. Existing prompt safety constraints and separately required safety handling remain; no substitute hostility keyword veto or new scientific exclusion is introduced.

eligibility.implementation: Frozen V3 scorer; four automatic quality exclusions. Hostility is descriptive only. Numeric and evidence rules retained.

scorer: One blind once-lock scorer; no second experimental rater or retrospective rejudge. Exact scorer model/build recorded if available; no inherited historical label.
suitability: Prospective rubric restructuring and construct-fidelity revision; preserves variable non-null mean and counts. This does not establish validity or equal psychological scales.

approved_eligibility_amendment.change: Hostility removed from automatic eligibility exclusion
